Subject: RFP: Dedicated reservation capacity worksheet and throughput targets

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our RFP for dedicated LLM inference, the procurement and infra teams asked that Redwood complete the attached capacity worksheet and provide answers to a short set of clarifying questions below. We need the completed worksheet back by EOD Friday (2027-04-01) to stay on our RFP timeline.

Quick context on expected workload:
- Production traffic expected to ramp to ~1,200 chat requests/min (conversational prompts ~150 tokens in, ~350 tokens out).
- Embedding pipeline: ~15M embedding requests/month (~250 reqs/sec sustained during ETL windows).
- Heavy reranking job: periodic batches up to 100k requests/hour.
- 99th percentile latency target for online chat: < 150 ms token-level tail as measured at the gateway.

Clarifying questions for the worksheet (please mark answers in the file and paste short summaries in the email body):
1) Recommended GPU families and quantities for a 24/7 reserved pool that meets the above throughput while allowing 2x headroom for peak growth. Prefer hardware options across H100, A100-80, and L4 if supportable.
2) Suggested reservation sizing vs burst/overage strategy (committed baseline + burst credits vs purely committed).
3) Typical per-token cost and token/sec throughput assumptions used in the worksheet.
4) Any constraints on model types/quantization that materially affect throughput (FP16 vs 4-bit quantized).

Attachments: Helios_RFP_Capacity_Worksheet.xlsx (we will upload to the Drive link below)

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if that would help.

John

Good questions — short answers:
- Chat is primarily multi-turn for clinical assistants, so KV cache reuse is expected for the majority (~70%) of active sessions. Average session length is 4 turns.
- Embedding ETL: we can tolerate a 1.5x burst for up to 45 minutes during off-peak ETL windows. Sustained business hours baseline should be ~200 req/sec.

Also: security/compliance note — Helios requires FIPS 140-2 compatible KMS integration for any private key management used with the private deployment. We'll include that in the RFP.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated reservation capacity worksheet and throughput targets

John — attaching the completed sizing workbook and a short summary of our recommendations inline below. The workbook has two tabs: (1) Baseline committed profile with per-GPU throughput rows and (2) Burst/overage model showing how credits would map to hourly bursts.

Attachments: redwood_helios_sizing_workbook.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)

Summary of recommendations (high level):
- Baseline reservation (24/7 committed): 6 x A100-80GB (baseline workers) + 4 x L4 for low-latency embedding fan-out. This mix gives predictable throughput for steady-state and is cost-efficient for RLHF/large-context workloads where FP16 is preferred.
- Peak/Headroom (burstable): 4 x H100-80GB available as burst capacity (on-demand or pre-warmed) to handle coupling of high-concurrency bursts and large batch reranking jobs. H100s are recommended for the largest batches and peak latency-sensitive flows.
- KV caching assumption: we sized conversational throughput assuming 70% cache reuse; if cache hit drops below 50% we recommend adding +2 A100s to baseline.
- Quantization guidance: For most open models we recommend FP16 in production for best latency/quality tradeoff. 4-bit quantization is supported on L4-class instances and yields ~2.5x token/sec improvement but requires model validation for accuracy-sensitive clinical prompts.

Throughput & cost assumptions used in the workbook (per-GPU approximate):
- A100-80GB (FP16 chat): 1.2K tokens/sec sustained; ~0.00055 USD per token-equivalent (workbook shows per-minute breakdown).
- H100-80GB (large batch/high-concurrency): 3.8K tokens/sec sustained for large-batch workloads; higher peak throughput for rerank.
- L4 (int8 inference / embeddings): optimized for embeddings ~350 req/sec per L4 (single-stream embeddings), cost-effective for high-volume embedding pipelines.

Reservation vs burst strategy recommendation: commit to the Baseline reservation above for 24/7 predictable traffic and purchase a smaller pool of burstable H100 capacity (or dedicated pre-warmed nodes) to cover expected spikes and the monthly rerank batch. The workbook includes a cost comparison for 12-month and 36-month reserved terms with and without burst credits.

Security/compliance notes: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS integrations and we can provide FIPS 140-2 validated HSM/KMS integrations for key material. We’ll include the SOC2 and encryption artifacts in the compliance packet.

Next steps proposed:
1) Review the attached workbook and call out any assumptions you want us to change (cache hit, token lengths, concurrency).
2) If the numbers look reasonable, we can convert baseline sizing to a formal reservation offer and provide a 30/60/90-day transition runbook.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive for Thursday or Friday to walk the workbook math.

Regards,
Irene
Irene Choi
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
